chapter: Later years and the Texas scene
title: Automatic players and developing a personal style
summary: Albert advises players not to depend on written music and to improvise.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: What do you mean by an automatic player? You've told me about guys that were just automatic players.

I mean this, that he's just... Well, for instance, what's his name? Tim. Tim says he can play, but he has to have music before him. That's an automatic player. He has to have it. I was the same way. Like I told you, you have to sit down and by yourself some time. And play the number that you read at first. And then try throwing it aside and try and play. Make your own improvisions.
So, little songs, turns, and twists. Yeah. Make you, you know, they'll say better they hear. That's sort of so.
So, get your own individual style. Something personal.
